headline: Thiel Fellow Sigil Wen opened an invite-only beta of Underdog, an AI assistant that runs entirely on a person's own computer so their data stays with them.
score_reason: Interesting privacy-first approach, but the launch was on 5 Oct, it is an invite-only beta, and the capability claims come from the founder.
importance_line: Privacy-minded users get an assistant that keeps data on their own device, but it uses a smaller model than the big cloud systems and its performance claims are the founder's own.
summary: TechCrunch reports that Sigil Wen, a Thiel Fellow, launched an invite-only beta of Underdog on Monday 5 Oct 2026, an assistant whose model runs wholly on the user's own Mac or Windows PC, with other systems promised. It uses a 27-billion-parameter model that Wen says compares favourably on some benchmarks with Claude Opus 4.6, a leading model, and the app will be free and ad-free, with the company taking a tiny cut of payments the assistant makes through Stripe.
notes: Launch was on Monday 5 Oct 2026 per TechCrunch, so one day before the 6 Oct window: score lowered by 1 (6 to 5).
